newsitem.title: UK: Animal lovers attack Taiwan over stray dogs.
newsitem.headline: Animal lovers attack Taiwan over stray dogs.

text.p: Animal rights campaigners on Tuesday condemned Taiwan for its "systematic and appalling cruelty" to thousands of stray dogs that are rounded up and left to die or killed.
The London-based World Society for the Protection of Animals (WSPA) said in a report entitled "Disposable Dogs: Made in Taiwan" that Taiwan was "one of the worst places in the world to be a dog".
The report said there were an esimated two million stray dogs in Taiwan, with more than 66,000 removed from the streets in 1995.

The report documents how dogs are, quite literally, treated as rubbish, being removed from the streets by binmen and taken to pounds where they are left to die of starvation and disease in overcrowded cages.
"WSPA investigators also discovered that dogs are routinely electrocuted, gassed, drowned, boiled or buried alive," it said.
WSPA said that last November and December it had visited 67 facilities for holding stray dogs. It classified conditions at 48 as unacceptable and described 12 as poor.
"The majority of dogs seen -- approximately 5,000 -- whether in old or new facilities were suffering with severe skin problems, were severely traumatised, with many close to death," the report said.
"Dead and decaying dogs were seen amongst the living, also dogs eating dogs. Humans at some of the sites seemed oblivious to the intense suffering around them," it said.
WSPA said the life of an animal appeared to have little value in Taiwan, where dogs were treated as disposable products.
"The management and fate of stray dogs must be one of the worst, possibly the worst, situations in the world," the report said.
WSPA urged the government of Taiwan to take immediate action to treat stray dogs humanely and said it was ready to help.
Hygiene and feeding should be improved and if dogs were to be put down, this should only be done humanely, using trained staff, WSPA said.
